date: Mecca, about 602 — the Conquest of Mecca, 8 AH (630)
title: 101cw1t
Who is Mu'awiya? His family, Abu Sufyan, Hind and Hamza
hook: Mu'awiya is the son of a house that drew the sword against the Prophet. At Uhud Hamza's liver was chewed in that house.
scenes.0.text: Mu'awiya was born in Mecca to a family of the Umayyad branch of the Quraysh tribe. His father was Abu Sufyan, his mother **Hind bint Utbe**. This family was one of the richest and most influential families in Mecca. When the Prophet started inviting people to Islam, this was the first house to oppose him the hardest. Years later, the House of Emmi, which would stand up to the Ahl al-Bayt, would come out of this house that had waged war against the Prophet.
scenes.1.text: After the Prophet migrated to Medina, the Meccan polytheists waged one war after another against the Muslims. After Badr, Abu Sufyan took over the leadership of the idolatrous armies. He led the army of Makkah against the Prophet at **Uhud** and at Hindaq. For years, he mobilized the entire power of Quraysh to destroy Islam and incite its tribes against Medina. This enmity never ceased until Mecca was conquered. The head of this house was at the head of the swords raised against the Muslims during the years from Bedir to the conquest.
scenes.2.text: **Hind**'s father Utbe, brother and uncle were killed in the Battle of Badr. Hind turned this pain into a deep resentment and waited for Uhud to take revenge. The Prophet's uncle promised freedom and a reward to a slave named Savage for killing **Hamza**. On the day of Uhud, the Savage, when he had the opportunity, threw his spear and martyred Hamza. This incident is told in Buhari by Wild's own account. One of the Prophet's favorite uncles had been martyred by Hind's wrath and a bounty account.
scenes.3.text: After the war ended, **Hind** came to the body of Hazrat **Hamza**. Syrian sources say he dismembered the body, removed the liver, took it into his mouth and chewed it. Then she made herself necklaces from her ears and nose. When the Prophet saw his uncle's corpse lying in this condition, he was filled with deep sorrow and wept. The Muslims were shocked at the sight. This atrocity against Hamza clearly showed how the house where Mu'awiya was born and raised viewed Islam and the Prophet's family.
scenes.4.text: In the eighth year of the Hijrah, the Prophet entered Mecca with a large army and the city was conquered without bloodshed. The Prophet said, "Whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house is safe". That's the word in Muslim. Abu Sufyan and his wife **Hind**, no longer able to fight, declared themselves Muslims that day. According to the Shiite reading, this is not a voluntary surrender, but a forced submission brought about by conquest. A family that fought the Prophet for years converted to Islam on the day of his defeat.
scenes.5.text: Mu'awiya became a Muslim with his father in the year of the conquest. The Prophet gave a share to Abu Sufyan and Mu'awiya while the spoils of the Battle of Huneyn were being distributed shortly after the conquest. This portion was given to the new Muslims whose hearts were to be warmed to Islam. The Qur'an says, "These people are the ones who will be won over". The Prophet was generous to them. But this generosity has not removed the family's hostility to the Ehl-i-Beit over the years.
scenes.6.text: The sources also mention a saying of the Prophet about Mu'awiya. The Prophet called him for a business, and he did not come to tell Mu'awiya that he was eating. When this was repeated several times, the Prophet said, "May Allah not feed your stomach". This is the word of the Muslim. Sunni scholars interpret this word in different ways. The Shia reading sees it as a warning, not a compliment. It is also said that Mu'awiya was one of the secretaries of the Prophet. But this man, who was said to hold a pen next to the Prophet, would curse **Ali** in the pulpits years later.
scenes.7.text: This family, who had led an army against the Prophet in Mecca, became Muslims with the conquest and soon became the most powerful dynasty of the Ummah. During Mu'awiya's reign, **Ali** was cursed in the minbars. The terms of the reconciliation with **Hasan** were violated. Mu'awiya left his son Yazid in his place before he died. The Prophet's grandson, Husayn, was martyred in Karbala by order of Yazid. In Uhud, the house that was hostile to the Prophet's uncle, Hamza, had drawn swords at the Prophet's grandson in Karbala.
sunni.0.says: Wahshi killing Hamza with a spear at Uhud.
sunni.1.says: The Prophet granting amnesty to everyone who enters Abu Sufyan's house.
sunni.2.says: The Prophet's saying about Mu'awiya, «May God not fill his belly», and the commentators' interpretation.
sunni.3.says: What Hind did to Hamza's body and the situation after Uhud.
shia.0.says: Abu Sufyan's enmity, Hind's role at Uhud, and the discussion of the characterization of Mu'awiya as a scribe.
disputes.0.title: 1q94d7o
His becoming Muslim and the scribeship
disputes.0.sunni: That Mu'awiya became Muslim with the conquest is told in the sources. In the Sunni reading he is a Companion and one of the Prophet's scribes; his earlier family background does not change his later ruling.
disputes.0.shia: That Mu'awiya became Muslim with the conquest is told in the sources. In the Shia account he is counted among those who professed faith while their lives were in danger; sincerity is assessed together with his later conduct.
disputes.1.title: 1qtjukm
Hamza and Hind
disputes.1.sunni: That Hamza was martyred at Uhud is told in both traditions. In the Sunni reading Hind later became Muslim and the Prophet forgave her.
disputes.1.shia: That Hamza was martyred at Uhud is told in both traditions. In the Shia account this pain is remembered as part of the family's earlier stance toward the Prophet.
questions.0: The Prophet said, "Whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house is safe". Why do you think the Prophet gave Abu Sufyan this order?
questions.1: The Prophet Huneyn gave a share of the spoils to Abu Sufyan and Mu'awiya. Why do you think this family's hostility to the Ahl-i-Beyt persisted despite their generosity?
questions.2: The Prophet said to Mu'awiya, "May Allah not feed your stomach". While Sunni scholars interpret this word differently, the Shia reading considers it a warning. Why do you think the same word is interpreted so differently?
summary: Mu'awiya is the son of Abu Sufyan and Hind, who stood against Islam in Mecca. The martyrdom of Hamza at Uhud is part of this family's past with the Prophet. The family became Muslim with the conquest. His being counted a scribe appears in Sunni books; in the Shia account it is disputed.
key: Hamza at Uhud and the family that became Muslim with the conquest
notes.0: Mu'awiya is the son of Abu Sufyan b. Harb and Hind bint Utba.
notes.1: Abu Sufyan was at the head of the polytheist army at Uhud and the Trench.
notes.2: Hind is remembered for what she did to Hamza's body at Uhud (sira sources).
notes.3: The family became Muslim at the conquest of Mecca (8 AH).
notes.4: It is related that the Prophet said, «May God not fill his belly».
